subject: Matrix of landmark coordinates for magnified shape change from plotRefToTarget?

messages.author: 1326f1b016745db2
messages.subject: Matrix of landmark coordinates for magnified shape change from plotRefToTarget?
parts:
Hi all,
I would like to know if there is a way to obtain the matrix of landmark coordinates after magnification from plotRefToTarget? I would like to use these coordinates for some other visualizations outside of geomorph.
I tried assigning the function to a variable, as shown here:
x <- plotRefToTarget(ref, PC4_no_allom_max, mag = 3, method = "vector", gridPars = GP_vector, links = links)
but this just assigns "NULL".
Alternatively, I'm assuming there is a way to calculate this myself? I'm not savvy enough with the math to know how to do this.
Thanks in advance for help with this!
Cheers,
Elena

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: Matrix of landmark coordinates for magnified shape change from plotRefToTarget?
parts:
Dear Elena,

If you type 
geomorph::plotRefToTarget 
in R console you can see all the calculations behind the plotting. The math you wanted is towards the top of the code, and this sections:

 k <- dim(M1)[2]
    mag <- (mag - 1)
    M2 <- M2 + (M2 - M1) * mag
 
basically they are calculating the vector between two coordinates, multiplying with the magnification factor (-1, since 1 corresponds to the actual difference) and assigning it back to the same variable. There might be a few more calculation in the rest of the code, which would be dependent on the dimensionality of your data and your your other parameter choices. But the gist of it is that.

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Matrix of landmark coordinates for magnified shape change from plotRefToTarget?
parts:
Elena,

 

Please see the underlying code. The magnification simply identifies the vector direction between reference and target, and amplifies it by the magnification specified. Specifically:
M2 <- M2 + (M2 - M1) * mag

Dean
